findings.text: def _stage_percentile is defined a second time at 4631 immediately after the first definition at 4617, character for character: the second shadows the first, so the first is dead and an edit to either copy can leave the other's behaviour silently in force; both came in with ebf70e3eda, in the commits gained since the review at 881e3fd9af.

_inherit_review_priority is unreachable: git grep over 789d5c72 finds only its definition and no caller in reckon/ or tests/, so ~30 added lines including a docstring stating that the review request is given the reviewed run's priority can never run; the write it performs (priority_override, priority_override_set_at, priority_override_reason) duplicates the capability reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:564 reprioritise already owns, without extending it, and the fragment itself says this node does not implement priority inheritance.

assert census["request_lag_seconds"]["max"] == row["request_lag_seconds"] compares two values the census itself produced from the same single sample, so it holds for any max implementation over one element and cannot redden on the regression it claims to guard.

assert row["launch_lag_seconds"] != row["request_lag_seconds"] is satisfied by launch_lag_seconds being None, which is the value this fixture produces because it records no review_admitted receipt; the request-to-launch interval, half the node goal, therefore has no assertion that reddens if the review_admitted mapping at recovery_review_dispatch.py:4694 is dropped.

The fragment quotes '10 passed in 8.3 s' for the node's tests at the head, but no log in the run directory carries that summary: the scoped gate log is at c10e31115a with 61 tests, the head arm reads '68 passed in 51.14s', and the only ten-test run recorded is the red negative control ('3 failed, 7 passed'), so a quoted figure has no receipt a reader can open.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_delivered_run_is_reviewed_within_minutes.py:167-174 recompute the lag from the journal and the negative control reddens three cases, but no assertion covers a real review_admitted receipt, so line 179 holds on a null launch lag.
justifications.evidence: after_suite-head.log records 68 passed EXIT=0 at 789d5c72627f and baseline_suite-head.log 58 passed EXIT=0 at 0c9f4fc8cd, and the negative control records 3 failed, 7 passed, EXIT=1, but the fragment's '68' figure is receipted while its '10 passed in 8.3 s' at line 73 is not.
justifications.fit: The block at reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:4600-4930 follows the module's commented-constant and docstringed-reader idiom, but carries two definitions of one function (4617, 4631) and an uncalled helper (4645).
justifications.goal_fidelity: The two intervals are reported apart at reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:4846-4925 and the obligation at 4849 reaches the duty rows via reckon/crew/resumption.py:3038, leaving only the surplus _inherit_review_priority as unimplemented prose.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:4645 writes priority_override against the owner at reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:564 instead of calling it, so this change both extends (review_stage_instants over stage_receipts.read_receipts, _stage_percentile over run_time_profile._percentile) and duplicates one capability.

verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit over 0c9f4fc8cd..789d5c72627f: the two commits gained since the review at 881e3fd9af are ebf70e3eda (101 lines in recovery_review_dispatch.py, 27 in resumption.py, 189 in the test file, wiring the obligations into report["reviews"]["failed"] and replacing the _nearest_rank quantile) and 789d5c72627f (19 lines in the evidence fragment); both also introduced the duplicated _stage_percentile at 4631 and the uncalled _inherit_review_priority at 4645.
